answers.contribution: Theorem 1.1 p.1 gives a dimension-independent four-cell equal-mass Gaussian noise-stability interval and equality classification. Beyond imported first moments, the contributions are quantitative moment alignment (Proposition 2.2 pp.3-4), the rotational kernel (Lemma 3.1 pp.4-5), and regret-normalized compactness (Sections 4-6). Priority cannot be established through this reading.
answers.mechanism: First-moment localization and closest-moment alignment; normalize transfers by actual OU regret; weighted tail control prevents escape; limiting facet flux has interaction determined by first moments; its only possible zero modes are rotations, removed by the moment gauge.
answers.hardest_step: Proposition 5.1 pp.7-8: arbitrary measurable transfers become L2 facet fluxes, with the sharp regret liminf (19)/(25) and interaction limit (20). Lemmas 4.2-4.3 and Corollary 4.4 pp.6-7 supply tail control.
answers.limitations: Qualitative small-correlation interval only; no explicit threshold and no conclusion at every positive correlation (Section 7 p.9).
answers.verification_obstacles: Imported Proposition 2.1 depends on Zhang first-moment and covariance results, including singular endpoints and price regularity; Theorem 1.1 additionally imports Heilman-Tarter existence and dimension reduction. Their proofs cannot be checked from this PDF alone.

mechanism_checks.normalization: With s_m^2=L_rho/rho, rho*s_m^2 is exactly the regret; (15)/(27) give normalized interaction at least 2. The saturated margin makes regret positive for every aligned nonidentical partition.
mechanism_checks.tails: The weighted transfer estimate and (11) yield uniform weighted tightness (21), with no relation needed between s_m and rho_m. The weight dominates first moments and the normalized Mehler kernel.
mechanism_checks.flux_coefficient: The density bound m^2/(2*phi_0), theta=m/(s_m*phi_0) and dnu=phi_0*dgamma_2 give ell/2. Exact vanishing on the pair plane makes the normal-score error multiplicative even for exceptionally thin transfers.
mechanism_checks.interaction_limit: Weak L2 limits, normal collapse (23), weighted tightness and compact uniform kernel convergence justify balance, first moments and (20). After replacement by x dot y the product integral factors into convergent first moments.
mechanism_checks.rotations: Closest-moment orthogonality is exact, passes to Df, and combines with the exact rotational interface kernel to yield the contradiction in Theorem 6.1.
